source_text: –Διάβλεψον, ἄνθρωπε, πρὸς τὴν φύσιν τοῦ πλούτου. Τί τοσοῦτον ἐπτόησαι περὶ τὸν χρυσόν; Λίθος ἐστὶν ὁ χρυσὸς, λίθος ὁ ἄργυρος, λίθος ὁ μαργαρίτης, λίθος τῶν λίθων ἕκαστος· χρυσόλιθον, καὶ βηρύλλιον, καὶ ἀχάτης, καὶ ὑάκινθος, καὶ ἀμέθυσος, καὶ ἴασπις. Ταῦτα δὴ τοῦ πλούτου τὰ ἄνθη· ὧν σὺ τὰ μὲν ἀποτίθεσαι κατακρύπτων, καὶ τοὺς διαφανεῖς τῶν λίθων σκότῳ κατακαλύπτων· τοὺς δὲ περιφέρεις, τῶν βαρυτίμων ἐναβρυνόμενος αὐτῶν τῇ αὐγῇ. Εἰπὲ, τί ὄφελός σοι λίθοις λαμπομένην περιστρέφειν τὴν χεῖρα; Οὐκ ἐρυθριᾷς λιθιδίων κισσῶν ὡς αἱ γυναῖκες, ὅταν κύωσιν; Καὶ γὰρ ἐκεῖναι λιθίδια περιτρώγουσι, καὶ σὺ λίχνως ἔχεις περὶ τὰ ἄνθη τῶν λίθων, σαρδόνυχας, καὶ ἰάσπιδας, καὶ ἀμεθύσους ἐπιζητῶν. Τίς καλ λωπιστὴς μίαν ἡμέραν ἠδυνήθη τῷ βίῳ προσθεῖναι; τίνος ἐφείσατο θάνατος διὰ τὸν πλοῦτον; τίνος ἀπέσχετο νόσος διὰ τὰ χρήματα; Ἕως πότε χρυ σὸς, τῶν ψυχῶν ἡ ἀγχόνη, τὸ τοῦ θανάτου ἄγκιστρον, τὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας δέλεαρ; Ἕως πότε πλοῦτος, ἡ τοῦ πολέμου ὑπόθεσις, δι' ὃν χαλκεύεται ὅπλα, δι' ὃν ἀκονᾶται ξίφη; Διὰ τοῦτον συγγενεῖς ἀγνοοῦσι τὴν φύσιν, ἀδελφοὶ κατ' ἀλλήλων φονικὸν βλέπουσι· διὰ τὸν πλοῦτον αἱ ἐρημίαι τοὺς φονευτὰς τρέφουσιν, ἡ θάλασσα τοὺς καταποντιστὰς, αἱ πόλεις τοὺς συκοφάντας. Τίς ἐστιν ὁ ψεύδους πατήρ; τίς ὁ πλαστογραφίας δημιουργός; τίς ὁ τὴν ἐπιορκίαν γεννήσας; Οὐχ ὁ πλοῦτος; οὐχ ἡ περὶ τοῦτον σπουδή; Τί πάσχετε, ἄνθρωποι; τίς ὑμῖν τὰ ὑμέτερα εἰς τὴν καθ' ὑμῶν ἐπιβουλὴν περιέτρεψε; Συνεργία πρὸς τὸ ζῇν. Μὴ γὰρ ἐφόδια κακῶν ἐδόθη τὰ χρή ματα; Λύτρον ψυχῆς. Μὴ γὰρ ἀφορμὴ ἀπωλείας; Ἀλλ' ἀναγκαῖος ὁ πλοῦτος διὰ τοὺς παῖδας. Εὐπρόσωπος ἀφορμὴ πλεονεξίας αὕτη· τοὺς γὰρ παῖδας προβάλλεσθε, τὴν δὲ καρδίαν πληροφορεῖτε. Μὴ αἰτιῶ τὸν ἀναίτιον· ἴδιον ἔχει δεσπότην, ἴδιον οἰκονόμον· παρ' ἄλλου τὴν ζωὴν ἐδέξατο, παρ' αὐτοῦ τὰς ἀφορμὰς ἀναμένει τοῦ βίου. Μὴ τοῖς γεγαμηκόσιν οὐκ ἐγράφη τὰ Εὐαγγέλια· Εἰ θέλεις τέλειος εἶναι, πώλησόν σου τὰ ὑπάρ χοντα, καὶ δὸς πτωχοῖς; Ὅτε ᾔτεις παρὰ τοῦ Κυρίου τὴν εὐπαιδίαν, ὅτε ἠξίους γενέσθαι τέκνων πατὴρ, ἆρα προσέθηκας τοῦτο· Δός μοι τέκνα, ἵνα παρακούσω τῶν ἐντολῶν σου; δός μοι τέκνα, ἵνα μὴ φθάσω εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν; Τίς δὲ καὶ ἐγγυητὴς ἔσται τῆς τοῦ παιδὸς προ αιρέσεως, ὅτι εἰς δέον χρήσεται τοῖς δοθεῖσι; Πολλοῖς γὰρ ὁ πλοῦτος ὑπηρέτης ἀκολασίας ἐγένετο. Ἢ οὐκ ἀκούεις τοῦ Ἐκκλησιαστοῦ λέγοντος· Εἶδον ἀῤῥωστίαν δεινὴν, πλοῦτον φυλασσόμενον τῷ παρ' αὐτοῦ εἰς κακίαν αὐτῷ; καὶ πάλιν, ὅτι· Ἀφίω ἐγὼ αὐτὸν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τῷ μετ' ἐμέ. Καὶ τίς οἶδεν εἰ σοφὸς ἔσται ἢ ἄφρων; Ὅρα δὴ οὖν μὴ, μετὰ μυρίων πόνων τὸν πλοῦτον ἀθροίσας, ὕλην ἁμαρτημάτων ἑτέροις παρασκευάσῃς, εἶτα εὑρεθῇς διπλᾶ τιμωρούμενος, ὧν τε αὐτὸς ἠδίκησας, καὶ ὧν ἕτερον ἐφωδίασας. Μὴ οὐχὶ παντὸς τέκνου οἰκειοτέρα σοῦ ἐστιν ἡ ψυχή; Μὴ οὐχὶ πάντων μᾶλλον εἰς οἰκειότητα προσεγγίζει; Πρώτῃ αὐτῇ ἀπόδος τὰ πρεσβεῖα τῆς κληρονομίας, πλουσίας αὐτῇ παράσχου τὰς ἀφορμὰς τῆς ζωῆς· καὶ τότε τοῖς παισὶ διαιρήσεις τὸν βίον. Οἱ μέν γε παῖδες παρὰ γονέων μὴ διαδεξάμενοι, ἑαυτοῖς πολλάκις οἴκους ἐποίησαν· ἡ ψυχὴ δὲ, παρὰ σοῦ ἐγκαταλειφθεῖσα, παρὰ τίνος ἐλεηθήσεται;
thought_title: Wealth is stones, a snare, and no excuse
orientation: Basil is directly addressing the rich hearer, urging him to see the true nature of wealth and to reject the excuse of providing for children.
pass_a_gloss: Look intently, [O] man, toward the nature of wealth. Why so much have you been excited about the gold? A stone is the gold, a stone the silver, a stone the pearl, a stone of the stones each [one]; chrysolite, and beryl, and agate, and jacinth, and amethyst, and jasper. These indeed of wealth the flowers; of which you the [some] put away hiding [them], and the transparent of the stones with darkness covering over; the [others] you carry around, in the precious [stones] taking pride in their brightness. Say, what benefit [is] to you with stones shining to turn around the hand? Do you not blush with little stones craving as the women, when they are pregnant? For also those little stones gnaw around, and you greedily have [desire] for the flowers of the stones, sardonyxes, and jaspers, and amethysts seeking after. What adorner one day was able to the life to add? of whom did death spare because of the wealth? from whom did disease hold back because of the money? Until when gold, of the souls the noose, the of death hook, the of sin bait? Until when wealth, the of war pretext, because of which is forged weapons, because of which is sharpened swords? Because of this [one] relatives ignore the nature, brothers against one another murderous look; because of the wealth the deserts the murderers nourish, the sea the pirates, the cities the sycophants. Who is the of lie father? who the of forgery craftsman? who the the perjury [one] having begotten? Not the wealth? not the around this [one] zeal? What do you suffer, [O] men? who for you the your [things] into the against you plot turned around? A cooperation for the living. Not for provisions of evils were given the money? A ransom of soul. Not for a starting point of destruction? But necessary the wealth because of the children. A fair-faced pretext of greediness this [is]; for the children you put forward, but the heart you fill full. Do not accuse the guiltless [one]; [he] has [his] own master, [his] own steward; from another the life he received, from him the means he awaits of life. Not to the married [ones] were not written the Gospels: If you wish perfect to be, sell your possessions, and give to [the] poor? When you were asking from the Lord the good-child [blessing], when you were deeming worthy to become of children father, did you add this: Give me children, in order that I disobey the commandments of you? give me children, in order that I not arrive into the kingdom of the heavens? Who also guarantor will be of the of the child choice, that for [what is] need he will use the given [things]? For to many the wealth a servant of licentiousness became. Or do you not hear the Ecclesiastes saying: I saw an illness terrible, wealth kept by him for evil to him? and again, that: I leave it to the man to the after me. And who knows if wise he will be or foolish? See indeed then lest, after countless labors the wealth having gathered, material of sins for others you prepare, then you be found double punished, for [the things] which yourself you did wrong, and for [the things] which another you furnished. Not than every child more akin to you is the soul? Not than all [things] more for kinship does it draw near? To [her] first give back the privileges of the inheritance, rich to her provide the means of life; and then to the children you will divide the livelihood. The indeed children from parents not having inherited, for themselves often houses made; the soul but, by you having been abandoned, by whom will be shown mercy?

lemmas.gloss: be terrified, be in a flutter

choices.term: Τί τοσοῦτον ἐπτόησαι περὶ τὸν χρυσόν;
choices.english: Why have you been so terrified about gold?
choices.why: ἐπτόησαι is perfect passive of πτοέω, 'to be in a flutter, be terrified'; the perfect conveys a settled state of agitation about gold.
rejected: Why are you so excited about gold?
Why so much panic over gold?

choices.term: Λίθος ἐστὶν ὁ χρυσὸς, λίθος ὁ ἄργυρος, λίθος ὁ μαργαρίτης, λίθος τῶν λίθων ἕκαστος
choices.english: A stone is gold, a stone is silver, a stone is the pearl, a stone is each of the stones
choices.why: The word order puts the predicate first for emphasis; 'a stone is gold' preserves the blunt equation Basil makes.
rejected: Gold is a stone, silver is a stone
Gold, silver, and pearl are all stones

choices.term: Οὐκ ἐρυθριᾷς λιθιδίων κισσῶν ὡς αἱ γυναῖκες, ὅταν κύωσιν;
choices.english: Are you not ashamed of craving little stones like women, when they are pregnant?
choices.why: κισσῶν is from κισσάω, 'to crave, long for' (used of pregnant women's cravings), not from κισσός 'ivy'; the participle modifies the women, not the stones.
rejected: Are you not ashamed of little stone ivy-wreaths like women when they are pregnant?
Are you not ashamed of little stone circlets like pregnant women?

choices.term: Συνεργία πρὸς τὸ ζῇν. Μὴ γὰρ ἐφόδια κακῶν ἐδόθη τὰ χρήματα; Λύτρον ψυχῆς. Μὴ γὰρ ἀφορμὴ ἀπωλείας;
choices.english: A cooperation for living. For were riches given as supplies for evils? A ransom of the soul. For were they given as an occasion for destruction?
choices.why: These are the rich man's imagined objections, which Basil quotes and then refutes; the short noun phrases are the objections, and the μὴ γὰρ questions are Basil's rebuttals.
rejected: They were given to work together for life. Not as supplies for evils, were riches given? Ransom for the soul? Not as occasion for destruction?

choices.english: it has its own master, its own steward
choices.why: The subject is πλοῦτος (wealth), referred to by the neuter pronoun; Basil says wealth has its own master and steward, so the rich man should not blame it.
rejected: The child has its own master, its own steward
He has his own master, his own steward

choices.term: παρ' ἄλλου τὴν ζωὴν ἐδέξατο, παρ' αὐτοῦ τὰς ἀφορμὰς ἀναμένει τοῦ βίου
choices.english: from another it received life, from him it awaits the resources of life
choices.why: The subject is still wealth; wealth received its existence from God and awaits from God the means of its purpose, so the rich man should not blame wealth for his own greed.
rejected: It received life from another, and from him it awaits the resources for living
The child received life from another

pass_b_english: Look hard, man, at the nature of wealth. Why have you been so agitated about gold? A stone is gold, a stone is silver, a stone is the pearl, a stone is each of the stones: chrysolite, and beryl, and agate, and hyacinth, and amethyst, and jasper. These are the flowers of wealth. Some of them you store away, hiding them, and you cover the transparent stones with darkness; others you carry around, taking pride in the gleam of the costly ones. Tell me, what good is it to you to turn your hand around glittering with stones? Are you not ashamed of craving pebbles, like women when they are pregnant? For those women nibble on little stones, and you greedily desire the flowers of stones, seeking sardonyxes, and jaspers, and amethysts. What jeweler has ever been able to add a single day to life? Whom has death spared because of wealth? From whom has sickness kept away because of riches? How long will gold be the noose of souls, the hook of death, the bait of sin? How long will wealth be the cause of war, for which weapons are forged, for which swords are sharpened? Because of it relatives ignore nature, brothers look murderously at one another. Because of wealth the deserts feed murderers, the sea feeds pirates, the cities feed false accusers. Who is the father of lying? Who is the craftsman of forgery? Who gave birth to perjury? Is it not wealth? Is it not the eagerness for it? What is wrong with you, people? Who has turned your own possessions into a plot against you? “A partner for living.” For were riches given as supplies for evils? “A ransom for the soul.” For were they given as an occasion for destruction? “But wealth is necessary because of the children.” This is a fine-looking excuse for greed. For you put forward the children, but you fill up your own heart. Do not blame the blameless one. The child has his own master, his own steward. From another he received his life, from him he awaits the resources of life. Were the Gospels not written for those who have married? “If you wish to be perfect, sell your possessions, and give to the poor” (Matthew 19:21). When you asked the Lord for children, when you thought it right to become a father of children, did you add this: “Give me children, so that I may disobey your commandments? Give me children, so that I may not reach the kingdom of heaven?” And who will be the guarantor of the child’s choice, that he will use what is given to him as he ought? For to many people wealth has become a servant of licentiousness. Or do you not hear Ecclesiastes saying: “I saw a grievous sickness, wealth kept by its owner to his own harm” (Ecclesiastes 5:13)? And again: “I am leaving it to the man who comes after me” (Ecclesiastes 2:18). “And who knows whether he will be wise or a fool?” (Ecclesiastes 2:19). See to it, then, that after gathering wealth with countless labors, you do not prepare material of sins for others, and then be found punished doubly: for the wrongs you yourself committed, and for the wrongs you supplied to another. Is not your soul more closely related to you than every child? Does it not draw nearer to you in kinship than all others? Give to it first the privileges of the inheritance; provide for it rich resources for life. And then you will divide your livelihood among your children. Children who do not inherit from their parents have often made houses for themselves. But the soul, abandoned by you, by whom will it be shown mercy?

fixed.note: κισσῶν is the participle of κισσάω, 'to have a pregnancy craving'; it does not mean ivy (κισσός), so the line is about craving little stones, not ivy-wreaths.

dismissed.why: ἐφόδια means 'supplies, provisions (for a journey)' but κακῶν is genitive of purpose/destination: 'provisions for evils' i.e., things that equip one for doing evil, not 'supplies for evils' as if evils are the recipients. The sense is 'equipment for doing evil.'
dismissed.note: 'Supplies for evils' and the proposed 'provisions for evil' mean the same thing; this is only a matter of style.
